notes.meaning: A wise woman strengthens her home through hard work, good sense, and care for her family. A foolish woman, on the other hand, wastes what she has through laziness or poor choices. By her own actions, she brings ruin down on her household.

Living an honest and upright life proves that a person genuinely respects and reveres the Lord. When someone chooses crooked and dishonest paths, their daily behavior shows contempt for God and His law. Our everyday conduct reveals whether we truly honor God.

Proud talk from a fool acts like a stick that brings punishment down on his own back. The words that come out of an arrogant mouth end up causing trouble for the speaker and hurting others. Wise people choose their words carefully, and their speech keeps them safe from danger.

An empty barn may stay neat and clean, but without a working ox, no plowing gets done and no crops are harvested. Real production brings mess and extra chores, but the hard work of a strong animal yields an abundant harvest. Doing meaningful work always requires dealing with some trouble and clutter.

A trustworthy witness refuses to twist the truth, whether in court or in daily life. A corrupt witness, however, breathes out lies naturally because deceit has become a habit. True character always shows itself under questioning.

A mocker looks for wisdom in vain because pride and cynicism keep him from receiving the truth. He will not submit to God or accept instruction with a humble heart. For an understanding person who is teachable, true knowledge comes easily.

Stay clear of a foolish person once it becomes clear that his words offer no truth or godliness. Spending time listening to corrupt and empty speech will only drag you down. Wise people do not waste their time trying to learn from someone who has nothing good to say.

The wisdom of a thoughtful person shows up in how he guides his daily life and duty toward eternal life. He acts like a traveler who studies the right path to reach home safely. The clever schemes of fools, however, only end up tricking others and blinding themselves to danger.

Fools treat sin and guilt as a joke, laughing off their wrongs instead of repenting. They refuse to make peace or seek forgiveness when they hurt others. Among the upright, there is goodwill, mutual favor, and a desire to make things right with God and people.

Every human heart carries deep griefs and private wounds that nobody else can completely understand. In the same way, the inward peace and joy given by God are too deep for an outsider to fully enter into. Only the Lord knows our hidden burdens and our purest joys.

The sturdy mansion of a wicked person will collapse because it is built on sin and pride. Even a fragile tent belonging to an upright person will stand and flourish under God's blessing. What gives lasting strength to a family is godliness, not brick and stone.

A path may seem pleasant, safe, and completely sensible to a person trusting his own thoughts. Yet when walked without God's direction, that road leads straight to spiritual ruin and death. We must test our choices by God's Word rather than our own feelings.

A person can laugh on the outside while carrying a heavy heart full of sadness on the inside. Earthly fun and wild parties often end in deeper loneliness and regret. No worldly cheer can cure an aching soul without the peace of God.

Someone who drifts away from God in his inner heart will eventually get sick of the bitter fruit of his own choices. A backslider leaves God in his thoughts long before his actions show it. A godly man, however, finds deep satisfaction from a clean conscience and the comfort of walking with the Lord.

An unthinking, simple person is easily tricked because he swallows every claim and promise he hears. A prudent person pauses, thinks carefully, and tests where each step will lead him. It is wise to look where you are walking instead of trusting every rumor.

A wise man holds a healthy fear of the Lord and stays far away from anything that looks like evil. He knows his own human weakness and will not play with temptation. A fool charges ahead with blind confidence, losing his temper and ignoring danger until disaster strikes.

A person who loses his temper quickly blurts out words and takes actions he will soon regret. Though a hot temper makes a person look ridiculous, a cold, plotting schemer is far more dangerous. People despise someone who quietly nurses anger and plans revenge.

Simple-minded people who refuse to learn end up with folly as their only life portion. They cling to foolish habits like a family inheritance. Prudent people, by contrast, seek understanding and wear true knowledge like an honorable crown.

In the end, evil must yield to what is good and true. Wicked people will eventually be brought low and have to beg for mercy and help at the gates of the godly. God ensures that righteousness will have the lasting victory.

When someone falls into poverty, even his neighbors and companions often pull away and neglect him. But a wealthy person finds himself surrounded by people eager to be called his friends. This painful truth reveals how selfish and shallow human friendship can be when it is based only on money.

Looking down on a neighbor because he is poor or humble is a real sin against God. Showing mercy and sharing what you have with those in need brings true happiness. God promises a blessing to those who open their hands and hearts to the poor.

People who spend their time plotting harm and dreaming up schemes are wandering far off course. Those who plan good deeds and seek to help others discover God's loyal love and truth. Generous plans lead to a secure and peaceful life.

Any honest labor of the hands or mind produces real profit and provides for daily needs. But people who sit around talking big without doing actual work end up in deep poverty. Success comes from rolling up your sleeves rather than endless chatter.

When wise people have wealth, they use it as an ornament and tool to honor God and help others. Their resources give them opportunities to do widespread good. But when a fool gets rich, his money only puts his foolishness on display for everyone to see.

A witness who speaks the plain truth can rescue an innocent person from jail, ruin, or even an unjust death sentence. A corrupt witness who lies brings disaster down on the heads of the innocent. Speaking up honestly is an act of courage that saves lives.

Fearing the Lord does not mean living in terror; it brings rock-solid trust and inner peace. A parent who reverences God gives his children a safe place to hide when storms come. God's protection extends as a refuge to the family of the believer.

Reverence for the Lord is like a fresh, bubbling spring of life for the soul. It keeps a person spiritually alive and warns him away from deadly traps set by sin. Honoring God is the safest way to avoid hidden snares.

A king's real glory is seen in a large, thriving population of happy and peaceful citizens. If a ruler oppresses his people or drags them into pointless wars, his population will shrink and his power will collapse. Good leadership is measured by the flourishing of the people.

A person who is slow to anger shows real wisdom and mastery over his own feelings. But someone with a short fuse puts his own foolishness on display for all the world to see. Keeping calm under pressure saves you from public embarrassment and sin.

A quiet, gentle spirit filled with contentment promotes physical health and vigor for the whole body. Jealousy and bitter resentment, however, eat away like rot inside a person's bones. Controlling our inner passions protects both soul and body.

Cheating or mistreating a poor person is an insult to the God who created him. The Lord made both rich and poor in His own image, and He cares for the needy. Whenever we show kindness and generosity to the poor, we bring honor to our Maker.

When trouble or death strikes the wicked, his sins pull him down and he is swept away without hope. The righteous person, however, finds a safe shelter and confidence in the Lord even at the hour of death. Faith in God gives courage when facing the grave.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern interpreters suggest the phrase refers to the righteous person holding on to integrity and courage in severe earthly peril rather than life after death.

notes.meaning: Wisdom settles quietly into the heart of a discerning person, where it is kept safe and put to practical use. A fool, on the other hand, cannot hold anything in and noisily blurts out his ignorance. The truly wise person does not brag about what he knows.

A nation is made truly great and respected through justice, moral integrity, and fairness. Sin and lawlessness bring shame, dishonor, and decay to any country. True national strength rests on godliness rather than military might or wealth.

A wise ruler takes pleasure in a capable, honest servant and rewards his loyal service. But his anger falls heavily upon an official whose laziness or corruption brings disgrace on the government. Doing our daily work with wisdom and integrity earns favor with leaders and with God.
